content: The consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations are being developed through a structured process. This includes addressing 19 key prevention strategies such as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), early initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART), and exploring individuals' experiences and preferences regarding HIV testing. If you are involved in advising or providing services for men who have sex with men (MSM), I will also ask for your perspectives on service provision related to the topics we discuss. If there are additional topics you would like to raise, please feel free to do so, as I will include any relevant issues in the report. It is important to note that you may decline to answer any questions or discuss any topics at any time. I would like to record our conversation to ensure I capture your input accurately and in detail. However, I will not retain any identifying information about you, so your identity will remain anonymous in the report. If you prefer not to have the conversation recorded, I will take written notes instead. In either case, our discussion will remain completely confidential. After our conversation, if you have additional thoughts to share, you are welcome to email me with your follow-up input. At this time, do you have any further questions or concerns? I want to emphasize that I am interested in hearing about your personal experiences and views, not those of your organization or what is considered legally or socially acceptable in your country. While you may mention differences in perspectives or settings, your personal views are of primary importance for this interview. Before we proceed, I need to obtain your verbal consent to participate in this interview. Would you like to participate? If you agree, we will begin the interview. If you decline, I will thank you for your time and discontinue the interview. Thank you again for agreeing to participate. I would like to start by asking you to share a little about yourself. How do you identify sexually? What is your living situation? What is your relationship status? What is it like for you living as an MSM (or however you identify) in your country? Regarding HIV testing, I would like to ask you a few questions about your experiences and those of others in your community. Where have you been tested, and in what type of setting (e.g., hospital, clinic, standalone HIV testing center, mobile clinic, community-based service provider, or self-testing)? Was it easy or difficult to access testing? What specific barriers or facilitators did you encounter? What do you feel is the optimal testing modality or setting for yourself and others in your community? Please explain the advantages and disadvantages of different options. What are the most important issues you see in providing HIV testing services for MSM? HIV self-testing is becoming increasingly available through online purchases and over-the-counter in pharmacies. Some countries are considering supporting community groups to supply self-test kits. What are your thoughts on self-testing for yourself and others in your community? For experts or service providers, I would like to hear your general thoughts on providing HIV testing for MSM. In your view, how has this been delivered most successfully? What are your thoughts on self-testing? How do you feel about current prevention approaches and practices? What interventions are you currently using to protect yourself from acquiring HIV or to prevent transmission to a partner? What barriers have you experienced in accessing prevention interventions, especially as a young MSM? What has assisted you in accessing these interventions? What additional prevention interventions do you think would be helpful for you and others in your community? What other strategies could improve access to prevention interventions? For each question, I may use follow-up probes to explore existing prevention programs in your country, their accessibility, and how they are received by MSM. I may also ask how you would organize prevention programs or improve conditions to meet the sexual health needs of MSM. Regarding antiretrovirals for prevention, I would like to explore your awareness and understanding of PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis). Are you aware of PrEP? Do you feel you have a good understanding of it, or would you like me to provide more information? PrEP involves the use of antiretroviral drugs by HIV-negative individuals to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Studies have shown that daily use of PrEP significantly reduces the likelihood of HIV infection through sex or sharing needles. PrEP is safe and causes few, minor side effects, but it does not protect against other blood-borne viruses, hepatitis, STIs, or pregnancy. Is this explanation helpful? Do you have any questions? How would you explain PrEP to someone else? What are your views on PrEP as a preventive option for yourself? Would you be interested in taking PrEP if it were available? What would help you make a decision about using PrEP as a prevention intervention? What do you think are the potential benefits and challenges of taking PrEP daily for HIV prevention? Similarly, I would like to discuss PEP (post-exposure prophylaxis). Are you aware of PEP? Do you feel you have a good understanding of it, or would you like me to provide more information? PEP involves the use of antiretroviral drugs by HIV-negative individuals after possible exposure to HIV to reduce the risk of infection. Is this explanation helpful? Do you have any questions? How would you explain PEP to someone else? What are your views on PEP as a preventive option for yourself? What do you think are the benefits and challenges of taking PEP for HIV prevention? Have you ever taken PEP? If so, can you tell me about the situation in which you decided to take it? Who offered it to you, and where did you access it? Was it easy to obtain? What was the recommended protocol, and did you complete the full course as prescribed? What was your experience of taking PEP? Would you take it again? If you have not taken it before, why not? If it were offered to you, would you accept it? What would help you make a decision about PEP? For service providers, I would like to hear your views on offering PEP to MSM who have had possible exposure to HIV. What are the benefits and concerns of offering PEP to MSM, particularly in relation to service provision and client needs? Have you ever prescribed PEP for MSM? If so, what challenges did you face as a provider, and what challenges did your clients face? What strategies helped address these challenges? If you have not offered PEP, why not? How many courses of PEP would you feel comfortable offering to an individual in a 12-month period? Finally, for community members living with HIV, I would like to discuss early initiation of ART (antiretroviral therapy). Are you aware of early initiation of ART? Do you feel you have a good understanding of it, or would you like me to provide more information?
